findings.title: Escalation condition excludes tickets exactly 48 hours old
findings.explanation: The code uses a strict greater-than comparison (`now - ticket.created_at > ESCALATION_AGE`) to decide whether a ticket should be escalated. The acceptance criteria require tickets that are "48 hours or more" old to be escalated, so tickets that are exactly 48 hours old are incorrectly left unchanged. This off‑by‑one boundary can cause tickets to miss the required priority increase. Also reported by compliance as requirement_mismatch: The ticket requires escalation for tickets that have existed for 48 hours **or more**, but the implementation uses a strict greater‑than comparison (`> ESCALATION_AGE`). Tickets exactly 48 hours old will not be escalated, violating the acceptance criterion.

evidence.quote: 1. An open ticket that has existed for 48 hours or more is raised by one priority level.

findings.verification_note: The code uses `if now - ticket.created_at > ESCALATION_AGE:` which excludes tickets exactly 48 hours old, while the acceptance criteria require escalation for tickets "48 hours or more".

findings.title: Rule: test boundary value missing
findings.explanation: The new behavior escalates tickets older than 48 hours, but the added tests do not include a test for the exact boundary value of 48 hours, violating the rule that every change in behaviour must be tested at its boundary values.

evidence.quote:
def test_an_old_open_ticket_is_escalated_one_level(service):
    ticket = aged(service, 72)
    assert [t.id for t in service.escalate_stale(NOW)] == [ticket.id]
    assert service.get(ticket.id).priority is Priority.HIGH
Every change in behaviour comes with a test, including the boundary values (for example "exactly 48 hours").

findings.verification_note: The team rule requires tests for boundary values (e.g., exactly 48 hours), but the added test suite lacks a test for the exact 48‑hour boundary.

criteria.text: An open ticket that has existed for 48 hours or more is raised by one priority level.
criteria.explanation: The ticket requires escalation for tickets that have existed for 48 hours **or more**, but the implementation uses a strict greater‑than comparison (`> ESCALATION_AGE`). Tickets exactly 48 hours old will not be escalated, violating the acceptance criterion.

evidence.quote: 1. An open ticket that has existed for 48 hours or more is raised by one priority level.

criteria.explanation: Urgent tickets have the highest priority in `PRIORITY_ORDER`. The code only increments priority when the current index is less than the last index, so an urgent ticket (last in the list) is never raised to a higher level.

assert service.get(ticket.id).priority is Priority.URGENT

criteria.text: Tickets that are not open (in progress, resolved, closed) are never escalated.
criteria.explanation: The escalation routine iterates only over tickets returned by `self.store.list_by_status(Status.OPEN)`, so tickets that are not open are never considered for escalation.

finding.title: Missing authorization check for priority escalation
finding.explanation: The public method `escalate_stale` raises ticket priority without verifying that the caller has permission to modify ticket priorities, allowing any caller to arbitrarily increase ticket priority.

dismissed.reason: No team rule or requirement mandates an authorization check for priority escalation, so the claim of a missing permission check is not substantiated by the provided material.
